newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli CPI-linked and unlinked bonds end higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli CPI-linked and unlinked bonds end higher.

text.p: Israeli inflation-linked and unlinked bonds closed higher on Tuesday but traders said the market was indifferent to the Bank of Israel decision to lower interest rates.
After trading on Monday the central bank said it was lowering its key lending rate for January by 0.5 percentage point to an annualised 14.7 percent.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.08 pct to 172.99
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 162.87.
Volume was moderate at 153 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds and Makams.

"The market did not react to the rate cut because investors had predicted that the central bank would lower the rate. This can be seen clearly by the moderate rise of the Makam," said a trader at Bank Leumi.

"CPI-linked long bonds continue to rise because there are no sellers in the market. Investors believe that yields will decline in 1997 and they prefer to buy bonds now," said a trader at Israel Discount Bank.

Unlinked bonds rose mildly. "It seems that there is a general consensus that 1997 inflation will be around nine percent. Unlinked bonds, which offer yields of 15.8 percent, are very attractive," the Discount dealer said.
Traders said the moderate rise of the Makams shows that investors are indifferent to the rate cut. "The rate cut was already reflected in the Makam's price," said the Leumi trader.
Dollar-linked bonds closed lower following the rise of the shekel against the U.S currency today. The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.266 shekels against 3.269 on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
